Agile Flier Th e maedrynn doesn’t provoke an Opportunity Attack

Far from removed from the terrifying murmur that slaughters anything under its shadow, a single maedrynn looks to be nothing 
more than a regular hummingbird. Only when threatened do they make their particular shrieking call, summoning others to flock in 
aid, their aggressive ripping bites begin to be reminiscent of their lethal mating season.
Swimming in shallow ponds and lakes that dot the great expanse of the Farplains, the aggressive nymphs outweigh any of their kind, 
capable of snatching fully grown fi sh in their grasping mandibles. Rapacious in the extreme, the nymph hunts and feasts the moment 
it hatches, rushing to not only escape the water and take flight, but to do so before hundreds of its kin do the same.
Born to race alongside its pack, the draffer cub rushes as quickly as its small legs can carry it to keep up with them on the hunt. While 
its tusks are little more than sharpened nubs, the cub learns from watching the pack how to encircle and harass the herds, to slash and 
cut to bleed them dry. Feasting on the scavenged remains, the adults often leave the rich organ meat for their young to grow strong on. 
Purposefully breeding only the most quarrelsome individuals to protect their quick moving herd, it is no wonder that the tartakka 
calves are found to be incredibly excited and playful. Often bounding ahead of the herd, only reigning back into the protective circle 
of the adults when their curiosity disturbs something large and frightful.
